name: Enoch
role: Who walked with God, and was taken
summary: The seventh from Adam in the line of Seth, and the father of Methuselah. Where every other entry in Genesis 5 ends with the man's death, his ends: he walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away. Hebrews reads this as being taken without seeing death, and Jude quotes a prophecy in his name.
body: Genesis 5 is a list of fathers and sons, each with his age at his son's birth and at his death, each closing “and then he died.” Enoch's entry is different: twice it says he walked with God, it gives him the shortest life in the list, 365 years, and it does not say he died.

Hebrews 11 counts him among the faithful: he was taken up so that he did not see death, having pleased God. Jude, calling him “the seventh from Adam,” quotes his prophecy of the Lord coming with myriads of his holy ones.

moments.text: Fathers Methuselah, and walks with God
Taken so that he did not see death

later.text: Jude 14–15 follows 1 Enoch 1:9, the opening of a collection of Jewish apocalyptic writings that George Nickelsburg dates from about the 3rd century BC to the turn of the era. Fragments of it were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls, and the Ethiopian Orthodox Church counts it as Scripture.
